scope: Physical W2 protocol validation and first app hardware integration. Version 0.11.0 is installed and discovery is verified; app-controlled output verification is pending.

appBuild.verification: Static analysis clean; 246 Flutter tests passed; final UI cleanup passed 40 affected tests; 10 changed/new screenshots reviewed; 12 HD7 and 10 discovery Java checks passed. APK version and signature verified against the preceding release.
appBuild.runtime: Installed as an update on Android 16. App discovery returned the expected W2 V6.02.232 32x16 profile. Device-password entry and app-controlled output acceptance remain pending.

artifacts.analysis: Local JADX Java/smali and radare2/r2flutter AOT inspection; separate from retained REA evidence

observed: Independent Android UDP discovery returned the W2 identity and profile.
Independent Church Service Timer HD7 login returned an authenticated 73-byte response and a 24-byte decrypted session result.
Clock calibration command 20 and file commands 2, 3, 4 each returned authenticated status 0.
W2 successful ACKs can be 41 bytes with an empty body and encryption flag C1. File-data ACK used C0.
A 393-byte native countdown program using the original Matrix glyphs was accepted.
User confirmed the countdown appeared, counted, was properly centered, and settled at 00:00.
Static 01:50 pause, countdown resume, AMEN cue and restoration transfers each received authenticated successful final acknowledgements.

User confirmed the repeated pause/resume/AMEN/restoration test worked as intended, then clarified there was one brief blink at each change, not repeated blinking while displayed. Full program replacement is functional but is not seamless.

Repeats using the same HP program identity for countdown, pause and cue received authenticated successful acknowledgements for every transfer. User confirmed the same brief blink at each change. Reusing program identity did not eliminate the blink on this W2. This does not establish that every possible controller update method must blink.

wire.request: HT, 27-byte header, BE total length, command, UUID16, messageId32, body, additive checksum16, AA
wire.legacyReply: HR, UUID16, BE headerLength16=28, command8, status8, bodyLength16, messageId32, body, additive checksum16, AA
wire.hd7Request: HD, LE totalLength16, headerLength8=23, session8, salt32, flags8, messageId32, command8, body, HMAC-MD5(16), AA
wire.hd7Reply: DH; same fields plus signed status at23; headerLength24; body begins24
wire.crypto: AES-ECB/PKCS7 and HMAC-MD5, as required by this controller protocol; no credentials in fixtures
wire.loginKey: Nonempty password: MD5(UTF8(password + 64ACFEB8B6FE4EF082DB8F3CD428EB20)); empty: MD5(32 zero bytes)
wire.completion: Require authenticated successful final fileEnd acknowledgement; this is controller acceptance, not optical verification

evidenceAnchors.program: classes.dex:F0.f; raw smali validates integer writes; p000a.b big-endian writer

integrationRequirements: Bind Android sockets to Wi-Fi explicitly, including when cellular internet remains active.
Select and validate controller identity; never treat simulator state as a physical connection.
One transfer at a time. Retries reuse the same request bytes, message ID and salt.
Invalidate confirmed-output cache after stale successful or uncertain in-flight writes, then reconcile the latest intent.
Clock/reboot recovery needs explicit verification and rebasing; do not silently clear uncertain session timing.
Preserve the original and square Matrix definitions unchanged.
Keep native countdown below 60 minutes until total-minute rendering is verified; app timer itself can represent up to99:59.
Do not change scan configuration, polarities, firmware, network settings or passwords.
